## What GEO is
Generative engine optimization is the practice of getting a brand named inside
AI-generated answers — the paragraph ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews
or Copilot returns instead of a list of links. It differs from SEO in emphasis:
entity consistency, answer-first page structure, structured data and
third-party corroboration matter more than link volume or keyword density.
It is also called answer engine optimization (AEO) or AI search optimization;
the three names describe the same job.

## The four published figures this practice is built on
- ~90% of ChatGPT search citations point to pages ranking 21 or lower
  (Semrush, AI Search & SEO Traffic Study, July 2025).
- An AI-referred visitor is worth about 4.4x an ordinary organic visitor
  (Semrush, 2025).
- Clickthrough for the top-ranking page drops about 34.5% when an AI Overview
  appears above it (Ahrefs, 2025).
- Email marketing returns about 45:1 in retail and e-commerce (Litmus, 2025).

## GEO vs SEO, in one line each
- What you win: a slot in ten links (SEO) vs a named mention in one paragraph (GEO).
- Measurement: keyword rank (SEO) vs citation share across a prompt set (GEO).
- Source depth: positions 1-10 (SEO) vs ~90% of citations from 21+ (GEO).
- Primary lever: links and coverage (SEO) vs entity consistency, extractable
  answers and corroboration (GEO).
- Time to signal: 3-6 months (SEO) vs 6-10 weeks for entity fixes, a quarter
  for citation share (GEO).

1. Read the revenue data with a model — cluster tickets, reviews and CRM notes.
2. Build the prompt set — 150-400 buyer questions weighted by revenue.
3. Fix the entity, then the pages — one name, one category, one claim; then
   answer-first rewrites of the highest-intent pages.
4. Earn corroboration — get named in the roundups, comparison pages and review
   platforms the models already retrieve from.
5. Convert it with email — lifecycle and outbound sequences behind the traffic.

items.question: What is generative engine optimization (GEO)?
items.answer: GEO is the practice of getting a brand named inside AI-generated answers, such as those from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Copilot. It works by making a clear, corroborated, machine-parsable claim about what a business is and what it is best at, then making sure that claim exists on the pages those systems retrieve from. It is sometimes called answer engine optimization (AEO) or AI search optimization, and the three names describe the same job.

items.question: How is GEO different from SEO?
items.answer: Search engine optimization competes for a slot in a list of ten results; GEO competes to be one of two or three sources named in a single paragraph. The practical difference is where the work goes: GEO weights entity consistency, answer-first page structure, structured data and third-party corroboration far more heavily than link volume or keyword density. Semrush found around 90% of ChatGPT search citations go to pages ranking 21 or lower, which is why page-one rankings alone do not carry over.

items.question: How long does it take to get cited by ChatGPT?
items.answer: First movement usually shows in six to ten weeks, and a meaningful change in citation share takes a full quarter. The fastest wins come from fixing entity inconsistency — one name, one category, one claim across your site, schema and third-party profiles — because models hedge or miscategorise you while sources disagree. Content and corroboration compound more slowly, which is why retainers here run six months minimum.

items.question: What does GEO cost?
items.answer: A fixed-scope visibility audit is $4,500 and takes three weeks. The ongoing Answer Engine Program is $9,800 a month with a six-month minimum, and the email-focused Owned Channel Build is $6,400 a month with a three-month minimum. Pricing is a starting point — scope sets the final number, and no retainer starts without a revenue baseline so both sides can tell whether the work moved anything.

items.question: How do you measure AI search visibility?
items.answer: With a prompt set, not a keyword list. We define 150 to 400 real buyer questions, weight each by the revenue of the customers who ask it, then run them against ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews on a schedule and record whether the brand is cited and in what position. That citation data is joined to the CRM so the report shows revenue, not mentions.

items.question: Can you guarantee my brand will be cited?
items.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. Retrieval indexes are not under any practitioner's control. What I guarantee is the inputs — the prompt set, the entity fixes, the extractable pages, the corroboration outreach and the email sequences — and honest monthly reporting on the outputs, including the months where a number moves the wrong way.

items.question: Do I need SEO if I am doing GEO?
items.answer: Yes, and they are cheaper run together. Technical health, crawlability and content structure are shared inputs: a page an assistant cannot parse is usually a page a crawler handles badly too. Ahrefs measured a 34.5% clickthrough drop for top-ranking pages once an AI Overview appears, so classic rankings still matter — they just no longer finish the job on their own.

items.question: How do I get my website into ChatGPT’s results?
items.answer: You do not submit to it — you become retrievable. Three things decide it: your pages must be crawlable by the AI user agents (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and the rest, which many sites block by accident through a CDN rule), your claims must be stated in an extractable form rather than buried in narrative, and independent sources must corroborate them. In practice the blocked-crawler check takes ten minutes and resolves more cases than anything else I do.

items.question: Which AI search engines actually matter for my business?
items.answer: Google AI Overviews first, because volume is not close — they appeared on roughly a quarter of all searches at 2025’s peak. ChatGPT second, because its users skew commercial and it drives the highest-intent referrals. Perplexity third for B2B and research-heavy categories. Copilot matters if you sell to enterprises on Microsoft 365. All four are tracked on the scoreboard regardless, because a brand that is retrievable for one is usually retrievable for the others.

items.question: Does GEO work for local and multi-location businesses?
items.answer: It works particularly well, because local answers depend more on entity data than on content. Assistants building a local shortlist lean on your name, address, category and hours as they appear across your site, your schema and the directories — and those disagree at almost every multi-location business I audit. Reconciling them is unglamorous and usually the single highest-yield fix on the list.

items.question: Is llms.txt worth adding to my site?
items.answer: Add it, but expect nothing from it on its own. It is a plain-text index of your best pages at the root of your domain, it takes an hour, and support across the major assistants is inconsistent. It is not a ranking factor and it does not compensate for an unclear entity or unextractable pages. This site has one; it is the least important thing on it.

items.question: How much organic traffic will I lose to AI Overviews?
items.answer: Model roughly a third off your top-ranking informational pages where an AI Overview appears — Ahrefs measured a 34.5% clickthrough drop. Commercial and transactional queries are hit less, and AI Overview prevalence in your category matters more than the average. The compensation is that what still arrives converts far better: AI-referred visitors are worth about 4.4× an ordinary organic visitor, so the traffic chart falls while revenue per session rises.

items.question: How much does GEO cost?
items.answer: A fixed-scope visibility audit is $4,500 and takes three weeks; the ongoing Answer Engine Program is $9,800 a month on a six-month minimum. Almost nobody publishes rates for this work, because almost every guide to it is written by a company selling software rather than the service. As a sanity check: below roughly $3,000 a month the daily tracking across four engines does not fit in the budget, so what you are buying is content volume with a new label on it. Full breakdown in the pricing table.

items.question: My brand gets cited but the AI still recommends a competitor. Why?
items.answer: Because citation and recommendation are different outcomes, and only one of them is worth money. Ahrefs read 9,886 AI answers across four engines in 2026 and found that 43% of the answers citing their own page never mentioned their brand at all — the model used the source and named someone else out of it. It usually means your page states the category clearly and your differentiator vaguely, so a retriever lifting one passage gets the category from you and the recommendation from whoever else is named nearby. The fix is to put the differentiator in the same paragraph as the category term, and to get third parties saying it too.

items.question: Is a GEO audit worth it before committing to a retainer?
items.answer: It is the only responsible order, and it is what I insist on. Without a baseline nobody can tell month six from month one, and every claim about improvement becomes unfalsifiable. The audit produces the prompt set, the current citation share per engine, the entity conflicts, a technical read and a ranked fix list with a revenue estimate per item — which is enough to do the highest-value work yourself if you want to. It is credited against the first month if you continue.

items.question: How often should AI visibility be measured?
items.answer: Daily, and this is not a preference. In the Ahrefs experiment a cited page appeared on only about one day in three between its first and last appearance, so a single spot-check has roughly a one-in-three chance of describing your actual position. Anyone reporting AI visibility from a monthly manual check is reporting noise. The scoreboard here runs the full prompt set on a schedule and reports the trend, not a reading.

items.question: Can I do this in-house instead of hiring you?
items.answer: The entity work, yes — and you should start today whether or not we ever speak. Pick one name, one category and one claim, then make your site, your schema and your top twenty third-party profiles agree. What is genuinely hard to run in-house is the measurement: a weighted prompt set scored across four engines on a schedule and joined to your CRM is a build, not a spreadsheet, and without it you cannot tell a real gain from a reroll of the same question.

items.question: What is the difference between GEO and SEO?
items.answer: SEO competes for a slot in a list of ten links. GEO competes to be one of two or three sources named inside a single generated paragraph. The practical difference is where effort goes: GEO weights entity consistency, answer-first page structure, structured data and third-party corroboration far more heavily than link volume or keyword coverage. The measurement differs too — a keyword has a rank, but an assistant's answer varies per user, so the unit becomes citation share across a fixed set of buyer questions.

items.question: Is SEO dead because of AI search?
items.answer: No, and anyone saying so is selling something. Ahrefs measured a 34.5% clickthrough drop for top-ranking pages once an AI Overview appears, which is a serious cut but not an extinction. Classic rankings still deliver most commercial traffic for most businesses. What changed is that finishing SEO no longer finishes the job: the same ranking now returns roughly two-thirds of what it used to, and the paragraph above it is being answered by somebody.

items.question: Do I need to do both GEO and SEO?
items.answer: Yes, and they are cheaper run together than separately. Technical health, crawlability and clean information architecture are shared inputs — a page an assistant cannot parse is almost always a page a crawler handles badly too. The mistake is not doing SEO; it is assuming the two programmes are the same programme with a different name on the invoice.

items.question: Does ranking on page one help me get cited by AI?
items.answer: Less than you would expect. Semrush found roughly 90% of ChatGPT search citations point at pages ranking 21 or lower, and its separate study of 200,000 keywords found AI Overview links overlap the organic top ten only 20 to 26% of the time. Two different engines, two different methodologies, the same conclusion: the retrieval pool and page one are largely different sets of pages.

items.question: What transfers from an existing SEO programme?
items.answer: Technical health, crawlability, site speed, internal linking and any genuinely useful long-form content all carry over and are worth having. What does not transfer is anything built purely to hold a ranking — keyword-stuffed pages, thin location variants and content written to a word count. Those tend to be actively unhelpful, because they give a retriever more of your site to sift and nothing quotable to lift.

A retriever lifts a passage, not a page.

layout.lede: Every term below gets used loosely somewhere on the internet. These are the meanings I use in reports, so there is never any ambiguity about what a number refers to — and each one says how it is actually measured, which is where most definitions stop short.

terms.definition: The practice of getting a brand named inside AI-generated answers — the paragraph ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews or Copilot returns instead of a list of links. Distinct from SEO in that the target is a sentence in a paragraph rather than a position in a list.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: It is the discipline everything else on this page belongs to. Also called answer engine optimization or AI search optimization; the three names describe the same job.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: By citation share and recommendation rate across a defined prompt set.

terms.definition: A synonym for GEO, more common in B2B marketing teams. Where the two are distinguished at all, AEO usually implies the narrower job of formatting content so a machine can lift a direct answer from it.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: Mostly a vocabulary difference. If a vendor claims a methodological distinction between GEO and AEO, ask them to state it in one sentence.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: Identically to GEO.

terms.definition: The percentage of prompts in a defined set where a brand is named or linked in the generated answer.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: The primary scoreboard metric, and the one most tools report. On its own it is misleading — see recommendation rate.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: Prompts cited ÷ prompts tracked, per engine, weighted by the revenue behind each prompt.

terms.definition: The share of prompts where a brand is named as the answer rather than used as a footnote.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: The more valuable of the two numbers and the one that correlates with pipeline. Ahrefs found 43% of answers citing a page never mentioned that page's brand — a gap invisible to citation share alone.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: Prompts recommended ÷ prompts tracked. Tracked separately from citation, and joined to the CRM.

terms.definition: A fixed list of 150–400 real buyer questions, each weighted by the revenue of the customers who ask it.

notes.label: Why it matters

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: Built from support tickets, reviews and won/lost CRM notes, clustered by a model, then weighted by revenue.

terms.definition: The machine-readable identity of a business: its name, category, location, offering and relationships, as expressed consistently across your site, your schema and every third-party profile.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: Models hedge or miscategorise you while those sources disagree. Reconciling them is consistently the cheapest movement available and usually shows within three weeks.

notes.label: How it is measured

terms.definition: Independent sources describing a brand the same way.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: Assistants weight consensus above self-description. 94% of an established brand's new AI mentions came from third-party pages in the Ahrefs study, against 6% from its own content.

notes.label: How it is measured

terms.definition: The set of pages an assistant actually searches and quotes for a given question.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: The pool and page one are largely different sets: roughly 90% of ChatGPT citations come from pages ranking 21 or lower, and AI Overview links overlap the organic top ten only 20–26% of the time.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: By recording the ranking position of every page cited across the prompt set.

terms.definition: A passage written so a retriever can lift it whole and have it still make sense: the direct claim in the first 100 words, specific numbers, a named source, and no dependence on the paragraph before it.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: Retrievers lift passages, not pages. A paragraph that only makes sense in sequence cannot be quoted, and a claim sitting apart from its category term gets separated from it.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: By reading the exact passage an assistant quoted and checking whether the claim survives on its own.

terms.definition: How inconsistently a cited page reappears for the same prompt.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: Measured at roughly one day in three in the Ahrefs experiment. It is why a monthly manual check has about a one-in-three chance of describing your real position.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: Days appearing ÷ eligible days, between a page's first and last appearance for a prompt.

terms.definition: Google's generated answer above the organic results.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: It appeared on 6.49% of searches in January 2025 and 24.61% by July, and cuts clickthrough for the top-ranking page by about 34.5% when present. Your ranking can hold still while the traffic behind it drains.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: By AI Overview prevalence across your tracked keyword set, and clickthrough on affected terms.

terms.definition: A plain-text file at the root of a site listing its most useful pages for language models, in the spirit of robots.txt.

notes.label: Why it matters
notes.text: Support is inconsistent and it is not a ranking factor. Genuinely low priority — worth an hour, after the items above, not before.

notes.label: How it is measured
notes.text: Not meaningfully measurable in isolation. Treat it as hygiene rather than a lever.

children.text: The problem

Paid traffic was getting more expensive every quarter, and customers were arriving already sold — saying “ChatGPT suggested you” — but only 4% of the time. Asked directly, the assistants named the brand in 9 of 240 tracked buyer prompts. Two legacy competitors appeared in nearly all of them, not because their sites were better, but because dermatology blogs, forum threads and comparison roundups named them constantly and named this brand almost never. The email list of 61,000 was getting one broadcast a week and contributing 11% of revenue.
What the model found

Claude is run over 14 months of support tickets, reviews and live-chat transcripts to cluster what customers actually asked — producing the 240-prompt set and, separately, revealing that three quarters of repeat-purchase language clustered around one question the email program never answered. That finding drives the regimen-builder sequence.
The plays
Cluster the customer data with a model
14 months of tickets, reviews and chat logs grouped by an LLM into 240 buyer questions, each weighted by the revenue of the customers who asked it. Prioritisation follows revenue, not search volume.
Rewrite 34 pages to be extractable

Direct answer in the first 80 words, a defined-terms block, a strength-comparison table with real percentages, and an explicit “who this is not for” section. Retrievers lift whole chunks, so the chunks have to stand alone.
Fix the entity graph
Product schema with real ingredient concentrations, Organization schema with consistent founding claims, and matching category language on Wikidata, Crunchbase and every retailer listing.
Earn corroboration where models look
Placement in 21 comparison roundups and review platforms, plus 6 practitioner-authored guides — mentions that put the brand name next to the category on pages ranking well outside the top ten.
Build the email engine on top

AI-referred visitors convert far better than paid but bounce on first visit. A regimen-builder welcome flow, replenishment timing per SKU and behaviour-based segmentation take email from 11% to 29% of revenue — built on self-hosted Listmonk with the segmentation done in SQL against the order table, because the timing model needs per-customer order intervals a hosted tool will not expose.
The lever

The comparison tables. Assistants answering “which is better for X” need something to compare, and a page that lays out the trade-off honestly — including where a competitor wins — gets retrieved far more than a page that only claims to be best. Second lever, quieter: the replenishment timing only worked because the order history sat in a Postgres table we could query directly — that model is not expressible in a hosted email tool’s segment builder.
How the model was calibrated

Calibrated on three published findings. Semrush puts ~90% of ChatGPT search citations on pages ranking 21 or lower and AI-search conversion at 4.4× ordinary organic. Its separate AI Overviews study finds AI Overview links overlap the organic top 10 only 20–26% of the time — the same gap measured a second way, on a different engine. Litmus puts retail and e-commerce email ROI at 45:1, which is why the last play is worth more than it looks.

Re-anchor the category claim

children.text: The problem

The previous setup sent everything from the company's primary domain to a purchased list with no verification. The ideal-customer profile is not guessed. A model reads every won and lost deal note from the CRM and returns the firmographic and trigger patterns that separated them, which cuts the addressable list by 82% and writes the first line of each sequence from the pattern matching that account.

Quarantine the primary domain

Move all outbound to four dedicated sending domains with correct SPF, DKIM and DMARC, warmed over 21 days. The primary domain goes send-silent to recover, and transactional deliverability is restored in week three.
Rebuild the profile from won/lost data
An LLM over two years of CRM notes returns the patterns that actually separate closed deals. 96,000 unverified contacts become 17,400 that match, verified and deduped against CRM.
Write sequences worth replying to
One observation about their business drawn from the matched pattern, one specific claim, one low-friction ask. Four steps, no “just circling back”. Testing on reply rate, not opens.
Instrument deliverability
Seed-list inbox placement monitoring, per-domain reputation and per-mailbox volume caps, with an automatic pause on any domain whose placement drops below 85%.

Replies routed by intent into the CRM with a four-hour response target. Half the previous program's losses were replies nobody followed up on.

Sending 83% less. Every metric that matters improves as volume falls, because the constraint was never reach — it was whether the message arrived and deserved an answer.

children.text: The problem

Email was contributing 9% of revenue and treated as an announcement channel: one send a week to the whole list, regardless of whether someone had subscribed that morning or churned eighteen months ago. Deliverability was degrading under the weight of unengaged contacts, and the two flows that did exist — a welcome email and a cart reminder — had not been touched in two years. What the model found

Order-interval data per product is modelled to estimate how fast each customer actually consumes it, rather than using the label's suggested duration. Reminder windows are set per customer from that estimate. This one change accounts for most of the churn improvement.
The plays
Model consumption per customer

Order intervals per product feed a per-customer consumption estimate, which sets each replenishment reminder window individually. Getting this wrong in either direction is the biggest source of avoidable churn.
Sunset the dead weight
A four-email reactivation attempt, then suppression of the 28,000 contacts who do not respond. Sending to fewer people raises inbox placement, and revenue per send rises immediately.
Build the flows that carry the revenue
Nine automations: welcome with a first-purchase path, browse and cart abandonment, post-purchase education, replenishment, win-back, and a pre-churn save for subscribers.
Segment on behaviour, not demographics
Sends keyed to purchase recency, category affinity and subscription status. The weekly broadcast becomes four variants of a weekly broadcast.
Test the whole flow, not subject lines
Offer structure, sequence length and timing — the things with real effect sizes — rather than another month of subject-line tests.
The lever
Replenishment timing. Nine flows ship, and the one that maps reminders to how fast people actually use the product out-earns the other eight put together.

Sized against Litmus’ benchmark of 45:1 email ROI in retail, e-commerce and consumer goods — the highest-return sector in that study, ahead of agencies at 42:1 and software at 36:1.
